- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.67), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); apply smoothing filter: cap 30d forecast max at 1.5x recent 7d high.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 0.67 → -0.67 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by -0.5 to -1.0 units to account for mean reversion.
- For 30d horizon, model often overpredicts late-period prices (last 7–10 days); reduce forecast tail by 1–3% to align with observed tapering or consolidation.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, model overestimates upside; apply downward bias of 1–2% to forecast if sentiment > 0.67 and price > 78.00.
